title: Canto 8: Withdrawal of the Cosmic Creations - Title, Artist and Source Pictures Canto 8
content:
Title, Artist and Source Pictures Canto 8

8.1

Title: Collage by Anand Aadhar against a background of a Brahma statue from Cambodja, Siemreap provincie, Phnom Bok, Bakheng style, end 9th beginning 10th century, Musée Guimet, Parijs.

Source: wikimedia.org.

8.2

Title: “Gajendra being rescued by Lord Vishnu’’.

Source: Internet. Additional prints of the Krishna Darshan Art Gallery.

8.3

Title: “Vishnu Rescuing the King of the Elephants”, India, Himachal Pradesh, Chamba/Mandi, South Asia, ca. 1675.

Artist: Unknown

Source/Courtesy: Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA), collections.lacma.org.

8.4

Title: The painting of Vishnu is a vintage Hindu picture.

Source: Internet.

8.5

Title: ‘Brahma Honors Krishna’. Page from a dispersed series of the Bhagavata Purana (Story of Lord Vishnu), India, probably Delhi-Agra region, ca. 1525-40.

Source: Internet. Philadelphia Museum of Art.

8.6

Title: A mandala of Vishnu. Jayateja, Pata/Paubha, dated 1420.

Artist: Unknown

Source/Courtesy: Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA), collections.lacma.org.

8.7

Title: ‘Shiva drinking the world-poison’.

Artist: Nanda Lāl Bose

Source: 'Myths of the Hindus and Buddhists', Ballantine Press, Oct. 1913.

8.8

Title: Vintage representation of Dhanvantari

Artist: Unknown

Source: Internet.

8.9

Title: Image of Mohini.

Artist: S.M. Pandit. The image was originally used for a Beedi cigarette advertisement

Source: Internet.

8.10

Title: ‘Indra Fighting Mahishasura, Vishnu Fighting Madhu and Kaitabha.’

Style: Folio from a Devimahatmya (Glory of the Goddess), India, Rajasthan, Sirohi, South Asia 1675-1700.

Source/Courtesy: Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA), collections.lacma.org

8.11

Title: Namuci swallowing the foam.

Artist: Unknown

Source: Internet.

8.12

Title: ‘Lady with ball’.

Artiest: Raja Ravi Varma

Source: Wikipedia Raja Ravi Varma.

8.13

Title: The painting on this page represents the different Manus.

Artist: Unknown

Source: The Hare Kṛṣṇas, harekrsna.com.

8.14

Title: The picture illustrates how Krishna may assume many forms, e.g. those of the Manus, to give instruction.

Artist: Unknown

Source: The Hare Kṛṣṇas, harekrsna.com.

8.15

Title: ‘A military parade’.

Artist: Unknown

Source: Internet.

8.16

Title: ‘Mahavira Giving Away Wealth’. The image is a Rajasthani painting of gopîs making an offering to Krishna.

Artist: Unknown

Source: Internet (Galleries of Shri Nathji).

8.17

Title: The photo (digitally enhanced) is of a relief of Aditi at Garhwa, Allahabad

Artist photographer: Joseph David Beglar, 1875

Source: British Library Online Gallery.

8.18

Title: Digitally enhanced painting is titled: “Vamana and Five Priests”, Number Five of the Vamana (Dwarf Incarnation of Vishnu) Suit.

Style: Playing Card from a Dashavatara (Ten Avatars) Ganjifa Set, Mid-18th century. India, Maharashtra, Sawantwadi (?).

Source/Courtesy: Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA), collections.lacma.org.

8.19

Title: ‘Vamana receiving water from a noble and his wife’.

Style: Marwar, early 19th century

Source: Internet © Victoria & Albert Museum.

8.20

Title: The picture is an Indian cave temple relief of Lord Trivikrama (Vamana).

Style: Date 600-700 c.e., cave 2, Badami, Bagalkot District in the north of Karnataka, India.

Source: Internet, Indian Temple Architecture and sculpture blog.

8.21

Title: 'Vamana' Tiruchchirappalli , c 1825.

Artist: Unknown

Source: Internet © Victoria & Albert Museum.

8.22

Title: The first picture of Lord Vamana with his foot on Bali is titled: “Dwarf Incarnation of Vishnu (Trivikrama)”. Nepal, Himalayas, 19th century.

Artist: Unknown

Source/Courtesy: Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA), collections.lacma.org.

8.23

Title: Contemporary painting titled: “Radha Krishna Bless Chaitanya and Nityananda Mahaprabhu”.

Artist: Unknown

Source: © Exotic India, exoticindiaart.com (used with permission).

8.24

Title: Digitally enhanced painted mural relief of Matsya.

Artist: Unknown

Source: Internet.
